correctness.rationale: PASS: The rooted-even-offspring Schur identity gives unit-determinant branch elimination over F_2[X,X^-1]. The two even-degree defects force odd side-branch counts on every spine vertex. The reduced tridiagonal presentation has determinant (1+...+X^m)^2 and is cyclic over the Laurent-polynomial ring; since its determinant has constant one it is cyclic over F_2[X]. Its module agrees with the m-site reversible path wave. Coprime primary factors yield all fixed spaces and exact period 2(m+1). The proof applies over any F_{2^f}; 102548 exact matching-polynomial checks and 96 independent binary dynamics instances support the formulas but do not replace proof.

value.rationale: PASS: The parity of just two degree-defect vertices determines the entire recurrent-state dynamics of an otherwise arbitrarily branched tree. The reversible-path-wave conjugacy yields an exact nontrivial clock, complete all-time fixed and primitive orbit census, and a branch-invariant periodic population; this is more than a routine small-table recomputation or a parameter substitution. One-defect trees are nilpotent, so two defects create a structural dynamical transition.
